text: The range consists exactly of values attained by the function at some input. It need not be the entire codomain, and repeated outputs contribute only one member. An empty domain has empty range. No inverse or choice of a representative input is part of this construction. Compared with [Faris §4.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L172).

The universal set contains every element of the specified ambient type. It is relative to that type, not a set containing all mathematical objects. No finiteness or nonemptiness assumption is needed: if the ambient type is empty, its universal set is empty as well. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1–3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L211).

The image of s consists of the outputs f(x) obtained from members x of s. Membership requires some such input, with no uniqueness or injectivity assumption. Repeated outputs are identified because the result is a set. In particular, an empty source set has empty image. Compared with [Faris §4.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L262).

The preimage of a target set consists of all inputs whose outputs belong to that set. The notation resembling an inverse does not require an inverse function: arbitrary noninjective and nonsurjective functions are allowed. It tests output membership directly, so the preimage of the empty set is empty. Compared with [Faris §4.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L134).

A set is nonempty when some element belongs to it. This is a proposition about the set, not a chosen distinguished member or an enumeration. It agrees with being unequal to the empty set, and can be false even when the surrounding type has elements. Compared with [Aspnes §§2.3.2,3.1](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L276).

Two functions are equal on s when they have the same value at every member of s. Their behavior outside s is unrestricted, so this generally does not imply global equality. On the empty set the condition is automatic; on the universal set it is ordinary function equality. Compared with [Faris §4.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L290).

A function is injective on s when equal outputs from two members of s force those inputs to coincide. Both membership hypotheses matter: collisions with inputs outside s are irrelevant. Thus a function may satisfy this condition without being globally injective, and the condition holds automatically on empty or singleton sets. Compared with [Aspnes §3.5.5.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L310).

MapsTo means that every member of the source set is sent into the specified target set, equivalently that the image is contained there. It requires neither injectivity nor surjectivity onto the target. An empty source satisfies the condition for any target, while a nonempty source cannot map into an empty target. Compared with [Faris §4.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L293).

BijOn says that the function restricts to a bijection from s onto t: it maps s into t, is injective on s, and reaches every member of t. Nothing is required outside s. The empty sets correspond bijectively, and one subset is empty exactly when the other is. Compared with [Aspnes §3.5.5](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L320).

This set contains functions defined on the entire index type whose values lie in t(i) whenever i belongs to s. Outside s, values retain their prescribed types but face no extra membership condition. Taking s empty removes the conditions; it does not create functions when their ambient type is empty. Compared with [Faris §4.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L279).

The singleton notation {a} denotes the set whose members are exactly the elements equal to a. It has one member regardless of the size of the ambient type, and introduces no ordering or multiplicity. Constructing it needs no procedure for deciding equality; membership remains the proposition x=a. Compared with [Aspnes §3.1](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L226).

The order notation s≤t for sets means inclusion: every member of s belongs to t. It allows equality and is not a comparison of cardinalities or a membership statement s∈t. The empty set is included in every set, and the definition applies equally to finite and infinite sets. Compared with [Aspnes §3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L90).

Intersection contains exactly the elements belonging to both input sets. The sets share the same ambient type, and neither finiteness nor decidable membership is required. Disjoint sets have empty intersection; intersecting a set with itself retains that set. The conjunction describes membership rather than counting occurrences. Compared with [Aspnes §3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L240).

Complement consists of the elements of the ambient type that do not belong to the given set. It is therefore relative to that type, not an absolute complement among all mathematical objects. Complementing the empty set gives the universal set, and membership is expressed by logical negation. Compared with [Aspnes §3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L113).

The empty-set notation denotes the subset with no members, represented by the always-false predicate. It exists for every ambient type, including a type that itself has no elements. This construction needs no chosen element, finiteness assumption, or equality test, and does not mean that the ambient type must be empty. Compared with [Aspnes §3.1](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L203).

Set difference s∖t contains the members of s that are not in t. The order of the inputs matters: this is neither symmetric difference nor numerical subtraction of cardinalities. The second set may extend beyond s, since only its overlap with s affects which members are removed. Compared with [Aspnes §3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L252).

Union contains the elements belonging to either input set, including those belonging to both. The “or” is inclusive, and shared members appear only once because the result is a set. No finiteness or disjointness hypothesis is needed; union with the empty set leaves the other set unchanged. Compared with [Aspnes §3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L233).

Inserting a into s produces the set containing a together with all existing members of s. It leaves s unchanged if a already belongs to it, because sets do not count duplicates. Membership means equality to a or membership in s, with no requirement to decide either proposition computationally. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1–3.2](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L219).

The Cartesian product s×t consists of ordered pairs whose first component lies in s and second component lies in t. The two factors may have different ambient types. Both membership conditions are required, so an empty factor makes the product empty; this operation does not multiply elements or cardinalities. Compared with [Faris §§2.3,4.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Operations.lean#L225).

Given a proof that a type is finite, this construction supplies an exhaustive finite enumeration without duplicates. It uses classical choice, so it is not an algorithm for discovering the elements from an arbitrary finiteness proof. The empty type is allowed, and no ordering of the elements is selected. Compared with [Aspnes §3.5.5.4](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Fintype/EquivFin.lean#L179).

An A-valued point is an R-algebra homomorphism O(GLₙ)→A. Evaluating it on the generic entries produces an invertible matrix because homomorphisms preserve the unit determinant. This is the point identification of [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W) for any commutative R-algebra A. WithConv marks the convolution group law on these homomorphisms; it does not change their values. Checks pass: [pointToGeneralLinear_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L77), [generalLinearToPoint_pointToGeneralLinear](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L173).
Matrix entries are evaluations on the corresponding coordinates.
Evaluation at the recovered matrix reconstructs the original point.

The (i,j)-entry of the matrix associated with a point is its value on the localized coordinate xᵢⱼ. The bundling equivalence leaves that coordinate unchanged. Thus this equation is the concrete evaluation rule underlying [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), for all commutative value algebras; no choice of additional basis or field embedding is involved. Checks pass: [map_genericMatrix_eq_coe_pointToGeneralLinear](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L87), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The entry formula identifies the whole evaluated generic matrix.
These entries carry convolution to ordinary matrix multiplication.

Applying an algebra homomorphism entrywise to the generic matrix gives exactly the underlying matrix of its associated GLₙ-point. The right-hand side forgets the stored inverse and its identities. This is the coordinate evaluation in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), valid for arbitrary commutative value rings because the generic determinant remains a unit under the homomorphism. Checks pass: [pointToGeneralLinear_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L77), [isUnit_det_genericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L503).
The two sides agree at every matrix entry.
The generic matrix has the unit determinant needed for point construction.

An invertible matrix defines a point by substituting its entries into polynomials and extending across the determinant localization. The extension exists because its determinant is a unit, as required by [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). WithConv equips this algebra homomorphism with the convolution interpretation; it neither changes evaluation nor replaces invertibility by mere nonzero determinant. Checks pass: [generalLinearToPoint_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L142), [pointToGeneralLinear_generalLinearToPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L164).
The constructed point evaluates polynomials at the matrix entries.
Reading that point recovers the original matrix.

The point constructed from an invertible matrix evaluates every polynomial coordinate by ordinary multivariable substitution. The polynomial is first mapped into the localization and bundled carrier; the displayed equality proves those changes do not alter its value. This is precisely the restriction property of the localized evaluation described in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Checks pass: [generalLinearToPoint_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L153), [pointToGeneralLinear_generalLinearToPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L164).
On individual generators, substitution returns the corresponding matrix entry.
The resulting evaluation reconstructs the input matrix.

Evaluating the point attached to a matrix on xᵢⱼ returns that matrix’s (i,j)-entry. The two coordinate maps merely place the polynomial generator in the bundled localization. This verifies the inverse direction of the point correspondence in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), using the input’s genuine invertibility over a commutative ring rather than a field-only criterion. Checks pass: [generalLinearToPoint_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L142), [pointToGeneralLinear_generalLinearToPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L164).
The stronger polynomial substitution formula specializes to this entry.
The entry equations recover the entire matrix.

Starting with an invertible matrix, forming its evaluation point and then reading the coordinate entries returns the original matrix. Equality of every entry proves equality in GLₙ; the inverse stored with a unit is uniquely determined. This is one inverse law for the representability bijection in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), over any commutative value ring. Checks pass: [generalLinearToPoint_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L153), [pointToGeneralLinear_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L77).
The constructed point returns each original matrix entry.
Reading a point uses exactly those coordinate values.

A point is recovered from its matrix of coordinate values. Agreement on the polynomial variables forces agreement on all polynomials and on inverse determinant powers, by [Stacks, localization uniqueness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM). Thus no information is lost by recording only matrix entries, even though those entries alone need not generate O(GLₙ) as an algebra without inverses. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_algHom_ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L667), [generalLinearToPoint_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L153).
Agreement on generic entries determines the whole localized algebra map.
Reconstructed evaluation has the original coordinate values.

Convolution of two points becomes matrix multiplication in the same order: evaluating Δ(xᵢⱼ)=∑ₖxᵢₖ⊗xₖⱼ gives ∑ₖf(xᵢₖ)g(xₖⱼ). This is the product law in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). The points are algebra homomorphisms into a commutative value ring, but their convolution group can be noncommutative; multiplication here is not composition of homomorphisms. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L597), [pointToGeneralLinear_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L77).
The stored coproduct has exactly the ordered matrix-entry sum.
Matrix entries are evaluations of those coordinates.

This identifies the convolution group Hom_R-alg(O(GLₙ),A) with invertible n-by-n matrices over any commutative R-algebra A. The forward map reads coordinate values, the inverse evaluates at a matrix, and the coproduct proves multiplicativity in the ordinary order. It realizes [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W), including arbitrary value rings rather than only field-valued points. Checks pass: [pointToGeneralLinear_generalLinearToPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L164), [generalLinearToPoint_pointToGeneralLinear](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L173), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
Matrix-to-point-to-matrix is identity.
Point-to-matrix-to-point is identity.
Convolution matches matrix multiplication in the same order.

The forward map of the group equivalence is the concrete coordinate-evaluation map already constructed. This equation fixes which isomorphism is meant: it sends a point to its matrix of values on xᵢⱼ, as in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). WithConv records convolution multiplication, while the displayed equality identifies the underlying function on points. Checks pass: [pointToGeneralLinear_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L77), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The forward map has the specified coordinate values.
That same map preserves the group multiplication.

The inverse group equivalence takes an invertible matrix to its localized polynomial-evaluation homomorphism. This fixes the inverse map in the point correspondence of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51), rather than choosing an unspecified group isomorphism. The unit determinant permits evaluation of inverse powers; the convolution wrapper does not change any resulting coordinate value. Checks pass: [generalLinearToPoint_coordinateRingMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L142), [pointToGeneralLinear_generalLinearToPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L164).
The inverse map evaluates every polynomial at the matrix entries.
Reading the inverse-map point returns the matrix.

For an R-algebra map φ:A→B, postcomposing a point with φ and then reading its matrix equals applying φ to every matrix entry. This is naturality in the value algebra of the functor represented in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). Neither injectivity nor flatness of φ is needed: homomorphisms preserve units, hence invertible matrices. Checks pass: [pointToGeneralLinear_toConv_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L237), [mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L254).
The equation explicitly unfolds value transport as postcomposition.
The inverse identification has the corresponding naturality law.

The group equivalence commutes with every R-algebra map between commutative value rings: on points the map is postcomposition, and on GLₙ it applies the map entrywise. Thus the bijections in [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W) respect change of values, not merely abstract group structures at each ring. This requires neither field coefficients nor an injective algebra map. Checks pass: [pointToGeneralLinear_mapValue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L227), [mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L254).
The concrete forward map satisfies this naturality equation.
The inverse group equivalence is natural as well.

Applying the coordinate counit to every entry of the generic matrix gives the identity matrix. The counit therefore represents the identity point of GLₙ, as in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51); it is not evaluation at the zero matrix. The source uses the Hopf structure stored in the bundle, so the result tests the actual selected coalgebra. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_counit_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L613), [map_counit_localizedGenericMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L261).
The stored counit gives one on diagonal entries and zero elsewhere.
The raw localized matrix satisfies the same identity formula.

The coproduct applied entrywise to the generic matrix equals the product of its left and right tensor copies, in that order. Its entries are the familiar sums ∑ₖxᵢₖ⊗xₖⱼ from [Stacks, GLₙ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/022W). The formula uses canonical tensor-factor homomorphisms and makes no claim that they are injective; it describes the selected bundled Hopf structure. Checks pass: [coordinateHopfAlgebra_comul_X](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Coordinate/HopfAlgebra.lean#L597), [pointToGeneralLinear_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/FunctorOfPoints.lean#L183).
The stored coproduct has the ordered generator formula.
Evaluation of this coproduct yields ordinary point multiplication.

Applying the stored antipode to the generic matrix gives its inverse, matching the inversion formula in [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51). Lean’s matrix inverse is defined even when a determinant is not a unit; here the proven unit determinant ensures it is a genuine inverse. The transport through the bundle preserves precisely these inverse entries. Raw inverse entries transport to the bundled matrix inverse.

Two algebra homomorphisms from O(GLₙ) agree if they agree on every generic matrix entry. Polynomial evaluation is then fixed, and preservation of inverses forces the determinant denominators, by [Stacks, localization uniqueness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM). The target may be a noncommutative semiring: this uniqueness statement compares existing maps and does not claim that arbitrary matrices define such maps. Bundling preserves the element; the displayed maps introduce no change of matrix basis or transpose. The counit stored in the bundled Hopf algebra agrees, on every raw coordinate element, with the explicit localized identity evaluation. The algebra equivalence in the argument identifies the same underlying element across the two presentations. This verifies the identity-point map of [Milne, AGS IV.1.8](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=51) on the entire localization, including inverse determinant powers.
